chunks: The (legislated) shares (of inheritance) cannot be more than six shares.

key_terms.السِّهَامَ: The prescribed shares (furud) of inheritance — the fixed fractional portions allocated to heirs under Islamic law
key_terms.سِتَّةِ أَسْهُمٍ: Six shares — the maximum number of distinct inheritance share categories: 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 2/3, 1/3, 1/6

ai.seo_question: How many inheritance shares are there in Islamic law according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) declares a foundational principle of Islamic inheritance law: the prescribed shares of inheritance cannot exceed six categories. This ruling resolves the jurisprudential problem known as 'awl (deficiency/excess), where the calculated shares exceed the whole estate. The original Shia audience, who faced disputes arising from such calculations, understood this as a definitive ruling establishing that shares must be reduced proportionally when they exceed the estate rather than exceeding the prescribed maximum of six.
